headline: PM Narendra Modi thanks Tarique Rahman for birthday wishes
summary: The Indian Prime Minister expressed appreciation for the warm greetings sent by the Bangladesh Prime Minister on his birthday.
details: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi thanked Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman for his birthday greetings.
In a post on X, Modi wrote, "Thank you, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, for your warm wishes. I deeply appreciate your kind words."
The message of gratitude was shared by the High Commission of India in Bangladesh on its official Facebook page.
Earlier, the Prime Minister's Office of Bangladesh extended birthday greetings to Modi via a Facebook post, wishing him good health and high spirits.
The greeting from Bangladesh included a birthday card featuring the Indian Prime Minister.
caption:
A diplomatic gesture of goodwill: PM Narendra Modi responds to birthday wishes from PM Tarique Rahman.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi thanked Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman for his birthday greetings.

In a post on X, Modi wrote, "Thank you, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, for your warm wishes. I deeply appreciate your kind words."

The message of gratitude was shared by the High Commission of India in Bangladesh on its official Facebook page.

Earlier, the Prime Minister's Office of Bangladesh extended birthday greetings to Modi via a Facebook post, wishing him good health and high spirits.

The greeting from Bangladesh included a birthday card featuring the Indian Prime Minister.

headline: 21 killed in 5 'golfing ops' led by Ziaul Ahsan, witness testifies
summary: A former RAB-8 deputy commander testified at the International Crimes Tribunal-1 that victims were hooded, handcuffed, and dumped in rivers.
details: A former deputy commander of RAB-8 in Barishal testified at the International Crimes Tribunal-1 that he witnessed five operations led by then RAB intelligence chief Lt Col Ziaul Ahsan in which 21 people were killed.
The witness, Maj (retd) Sabbir Rahman Osmani, described a chilling pattern where victims were kept hooded and handcuffed before being shot and dumped into rivers.
According to the testimony, operatives tied cement sacks to the victims' legs and necks and used pillows to muffle the sound before shooting them.
These operations were referred to as 'golfing,' with Ziaul allegedly telling operatives that the 'highest level of the state' was aware of the incidents.
The witness further narrated three 'staged operations' in the Sundarbans where 16 alleged robbers were killed in so-called crossfires.
Sabbir also testified that Ziaul ordered the elimination of a boatman named Alkas, who had provided his boat for the operations, to prevent operational secrets from being leaked.
Ziaul Ahsan is currently facing trial for the alleged enforced disappearance and murder of 104 people between 2010 and 2013.
caption:
21 people were killed in 'golfing operations' where victims were hooded, handcuffed, and dumped in rivers.

A former deputy commander of RAB-8 in Barishal testified at the International Crimes Tribunal-1 that he witnessed five operations led by then RAB intelligence chief Lt Col Ziaul Ahsan in which 21 people were killed.

The witness, Maj (retd) Sabbir Rahman Osmani, described a chilling pattern where victims were kept hooded and handcuffed before being shot and dumped into rivers.

According to the testimony, operatives tied cement sacks to the victims' legs and necks and used pillows to muffle the sound before shooting them.

These operations were referred to as 'golfing,' with Ziaul allegedly telling operatives that the 'highest level of the state' was aware of the incidents.

The witness further narrated three 'staged operations' in the Sundarbans where 16 alleged robbers were killed in so-called crossfires.

Sabbir also testified that Ziaul ordered the elimination of a boatman named Alkas, who had provided his boat for the operations, to prevent operational secrets from being leaked.

Ziaul Ahsan is currently facing trial for the alleged enforced disappearance and murder of 104 people between 2010 and 2013.
